en: The One Hundred Verses on the Collection of the Noble and Holy,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Imperial Court Rank of Chao San Da Fu,
Acting Assistant Director of the Honglu, the Great Master Mingjiao, the Subject Tian Xizai, by imperial decree.
I prostrate to all those who have transcended the world, The most honored ones in the three realms, oceans of merit;
With the fire of wisdom, you can burn away the stains of affliction— To the Perfectly Awakened One, I now pay homage with my life.

I bow my head to the one who can pull us from the perilous depths of birth and death, who universally dries up the ocean of sorrow, affliction, greed, and delusion, and who shatters the mountain of worldly toil and sinful karma;
I now take refuge and pay homage to the Jewel of the Sublime Dharma.
I bow my head in homage to all Buddhas who are praised, Who adorn themselves with the practice of the Eightfold Noble Path;
To those whose unconditioned meditative concentrations gradually become perfect and luminous, I now take refuge and pay homage to the Jewel of the Sangha.
The inner palace treasuries and various pavilions, With the manifold radiance of gold, jade, and mani-jewels,
And vast adornments of pearl necklaces— Where hundreds of thousands of devas constantly roam;
If one attains a secure dwelling within the celestial realms, It is the reward for having built and adorned Buddhist temples.
With faith and reverence, one takes refuge in the Triple Gem;
by bestowing wealth and silk within the vihāra, and having experienced the bliss of gods and humans, one shall attain the fruit of nirvāṇa and quiescence.
The vihāra, having stood for many years, is largely dilapidated;
by restoring and adorning it to offer to the Buddha and the Saṅgha, one will constantly obtain happiness dwelling among humans and devas, and shall also attain the fruit of nirvāṇa’s quiescence.
If one gives gardens and groves to a monastery, as well as seats, robes, and medicinal elixirs; and further,
when encountering an evil age of famine and distress, provides food and drink to those sentient beings—
one thereby obtains boundless merit and attains the seven noble riches of the wise.
All sufferings of the evil realms are eliminated, And one shall forever enjoy inexhaustible great wealth.
Regarding the places where the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, walk and dwell, if a person, having arrived there, gives rise to reverence,
serves and makes offerings while also hearing the Dharma, and with deep faith practices and trains according to the precepts—
One shall obtain vast and boundless fruits, Like the ocean, vast and deep;
Even with vessels to measure it, calculation cannot reach them— The causes and conditions of merit are likewise so.
If a person constructs a Buddha hall, Cold, heat, wind, and rain cannot invade it;
They shall first realize the Dharma of Nirvana, And fulfill all their wishes at will.
If a person carves or paints an image of the Buddha, they shall be liberated from sorrow, affliction, and disease;
furthermore, they shall obtain a sublime and wondrous body in heaven, as well as great wisdom, auspiciousness, and nobility.
If a person reverently repairs an image of the Buddha, they shall obtain a firm and healthy body;
long-lived, with physical strength and all marks perfected, they will later attain the tranquil bliss of nirvāṇa.
All anxieties, afflictions, and disputes will be eliminated; they will possess courageous eloquence and be praised by others.
Subduing the sense faculties and exerting diligence, adorned in every way, one is revered by all.
If a person cultivates the images of the Buddhas and so forth, they will remain far removed from faults and attain birth in heaven;
noble, dignified, and handsome, they will be esteemed by all, and all merits and virtues will be fully perfected.
If one repairs a damaged stupa or temple, that person will be free from illness and possess a perfect body;
all desirable fruits within the world will be fully attained according to their wishes.
If one creates images of the Buddha or Buddhist stupas, even if their dimensions are as small as a grain of wheat,
they will certainly become kings and enjoy happiness not only in the heavens and among humans,
but likewise in the realms of form and formlessness; their wealth and nobility will be boundless and immeasurable.
One shall leave behind the sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, and death, and ultimately perfect the Buddha-fruit of Bodhi.
If one places relics within a stupa or temple, or paints images of the Buddha to make offerings,
one will attain that ground of the Great Stage of Wisdom-Light and the pure, wondrous, and noble sovereignty of the Sugata.
Abiding within the boundless realms of sentient beings, They enter together into the nature of equality and signlessness.
If one places a Buddha stūpa and its parasol Upon a tranquil mountain peak,
even if its size is but that of a finger-joint, One shall be born among all humans and devas.
Stately, immensely wealthy, with physical strength and well-being, One shall later become a deva among the Thirty-three.
If a person opens a Buddha-stūpa with their own hand, They shall obtain wealth, nobility, and full perfection;
Their body will be radiant and pure, their mind supple, Possessing great knowledge, a pure nature, and free from malice.
If there is a wise person who practices the perfection of giving, offering the Buddha powdered incense, white sandalwood,
and various fragrances such as *kunkuma*, they shall obtain vast and desirable fruits.
If a person believes in the Buddha and gives rise to joy, offering exquisite incense, flowers,
and music as various kinds of worship to the Tathāgata, they will be reborn in heaven and experience a pond of gold and jewels;
with the fine, fragrant pollen of the lotuses from that pond, their entire body will be sprinkled and bathed.
The waters of the Manasvinī are pure and clear; those who enter find their defilements naturally removed.
Waves surge and flow, spraying cool fragrances, while jewel-banked shores are surrounded by blooming red lotuses.
Devas and others who behold this are ever delighted; such is the retribution for bestowing gifts upon the Buddha and the Saṅgha.
Such merit is immeasurable; therefore, the various sūtras conclude with verses of praise.
By giving famous garments and superior robes to the Buddha or to the Saṅgha, when one is later reborn in the celestial realms, one will possess the most sublime heavenly robes and fragrances.
With various colors such as blue and yellow,
and hundreds of thousands of mani jewels used for adornment, one attains immeasurable wealth and sovereignty,
as well as boundless happiness— reaping these supreme and wondrous fruits.
If a person is born into this world and becomes a king,
possessing all the marks of excellence, wearing garments of the finest silks and brocades,
and constantly enjoying various sublime and superior fragrances at his disposal;
All are due to the gift of robes to the Buddha, which brings about such rewards as these.
If one is born in the celestial realms, adorned with various jewels,
wearing pearl necklaces upon the body and a precious jade crown upon the head, it is for this reason.
With earrings and bracelets— such wealth and happiness—
by offering these ornaments to the Buddha, one obtains the supreme and wondrous fruits of the heavens.
If one becomes a great king, one’s physical form will be vast and magnificently adorned.
Necklaces of maṇi jewels, with their tinkling and resonant sounds, are likewise fields for the Triple Gem; they are ornaments offered as gifts.
With a pure mind, the wise person bestows flower garlands and other such offerings upon the Buddha.
In the heavens and among humans, they constantly obtain happiness;
having brought forth the flowers of the seven factors of enlightenment, they are reborn on the celestial and terrestrial realms as Śakra,
Lord of the Devas, together with their various retinues.
Sporting in the gardens and making offerings of various flowers,
one obtains such fruits as these:
canopies adorned with gold, silver, blue, and green.
Round as the full moon, like a king or a great minister,
it is used to cover the head; by giving an umbrella,
one obtains this retribution, and is liberated from greed, sorrow, and affliction.
Free from illness and ever at peace, one further becomes a king of the world;
this too is the retribution for giving canopies.
By giving banners and streamers, one shall become a celestial wheel-turning monarch.
Invincible in the world, having distanced oneself from all transgressions,
one becomes the foremost among all sentient beings,
constantly receiving the offerings of others.
By giving gifts such as bells and chimes, one is not born in lands of evil;
one constantly attains the Brahma-voice.
By offering lutes, harps, drums, and wind instruments to the Buddhas and noble sages, [one gains these rewards].
May their hearing be joyful and their minds delighted; they shall attain the faculty of the divine ear,
ever adorned and pure, and further obtain adamantine wisdom to shatter the mountains of affliction.
With exquisite forms, fragrances, and flavors, And various kinds of delicious food and drink,
One makes offerings to the Buddhas and others; Such a person shall be born within the celestial realms,
Where retinues share a single precious throne, And use vessels made of *maṇi* jewels.
One shall partake of the exquisite food of the heavens,
And never be born during the kalpas of famine or war.
By making offerings to the assembly of sages and worthies, One shall be reborn among humans and devas.
Delicious food is always abundant, of every kind and most excellent;
the wise always revere and love him.
By giving to those who have gone forth, one constantly attains a body of wealth and happiness.
Possessing eloquence and long life, with physical strength and all marks complete—
such is the retribution for giving food.
By giving them sweet honey-water, ghee, milk, curd, and fermented grain-drinks, [one gains these fruits].
Causing those who are parched and weary to drink and obtain peace and happiness,
they too shall receive a reward as previously described.
By offering forest creepers and various medicinal herbs to the noble sages, one attains such merit.
One shall be born among humans or devas, free from illness and long-lived,
constantly attaining physical peace and happiness.
Later, one shall be reborn in a celestial palace, where the flowers of the kalpa-tree are in full and fragrant bloom.
Whatever one seeks is obtained according to one’s wish: precious vessels, wine, honey, and the like;
kinsmen share in the drinking.
Adornments emerge forth, as do singing celestial maidens and heavenly music.
The hearts of the celestial hosts are gladdened, and ambrosia follows them;
by giving drink, one obtains this retribution.
One shall be born among humans or devas, far removed from poverty and cold.
Possessing long life and abundant wealth,
with carriages, vehicles, and palanquins, one who makes offerings and gifts to the Tathāgata shall attain great supernormal powers.
One will be born into a family of constant high standing, always possessing elephants, horses, and chariots,
forever free from the hardships of poverty.
If one serves with diligence, one shall, in all places, [attain these things].
All that is sought shall be accomplished;
one shall be reborn in the heavens, never undergoing bitter toil,
and shall always sit upon the most excellent seat.
Born in heaven, one is ever joyful; with a body vast, upright, and fearless, one is praised by others.
Adorning various dwellings and giving them to others for their use, one provides places for them to stay.
When body and mind give rise to joy and serenity, one shall be summoned to the Garden of Delight (Nandana),
a place where devas and humans roam; there, together with celestial maidens,
one shall sport and enjoy bliss.
By providing the gift of shade and coolness, one shall experience the Udumbara and Nyagrodha Bodhi trees;
furthermore, one will later be reborn in heaven,
constantly enjoying the pleasures of the five desires.
Adorning them until they are pure and radiant, one relieves those who are thirsty and destitute,
causing all to be fully satisfied; as a karmic reward for this,
one will be reborn in the heavens or the Brahma world, experiencing various kinds of bliss.
Furthermore, one realizes the fruit of nirvāṇa.
By making offerings to the Triple Gem, one shall be born in all places wealthy and happy;
within those worlds, [one shall enjoy such fortune].
Venerable, of supreme and highest virtue, you further inspire all sentient beings to constantly make offerings to you.
They shall be born in the heavens and attain wisdom that is most acute and sharp.
They shall never encounter the calamities of war;
their wisdom will always be fierce and sharp, able to sever all afflictions and realize that path of tranquility.
In the sculpted and painted images of the Buddha, one is born within the celestial realms;
with a body of true golden color and pure radiance like the sun,
there are the multitudes of devas, both male and female.
I take refuge at all times.
Skillfully bestowing the gift of the Dharma, one is born among gods and humans;
endowed with the power of wisdom and virtue, one constantly experiences happiness.
Forever free from sorrow, lamentation, and suffering,
one shall attain the path of nirvāṇa in a future existence.
By transcribing this precious, sublime Dharma, one shall obtain the knowledge of past lives.
Constantly enjoying wealth, honor, and peace, they extinguish all sins;
even after passing through ten million kalpas, they shall not fall into the realms of hell,
hungry ghosts, or animals.
Sweeping and sprinkling to establish the altar, circumambulating and scattering incense and flowers,
making offerings at all times, one shall later be born among humans or in the heavens, constantly enjoying wealth and nobility.
Furthermore, because they have realized quiescence, they make offerings to the Buddhas and noble sages;
they are reborn among humans and devas, and their three eyes are ever pure: the wisdom eye and the divine eye.
And because of their physical eyes,
they shall always be born in the heavens; their mouths shall never be mute,
and their ears and eyes shall never be deaf or blind.
It is not merely that the three eyes are purified, But that one can fully penetrate all the teachings of Perfect Enlightenment.
One should make offerings to those of virtuous merit, To śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas.
Giving a small gift yields a great reward; one extensively obtains the wealth that accords with the Path and enjoys it for a long time.
By giving food to the classes of animals, the merit obtained is as follows:
It results in a hundredfold increase.
By giving to those who have committed offenses, merit and benefit gradually become even more distinguished,
and one obtains blessings a thousandfold.
One who makes offerings to those free from conceptual mind gains a thousandfold or ten-thousandfold merit;
as for those who are no longer subject to training (aśaikṣa), the merit obtained is a hundred koṭis.
Surpassing all others,
one shall be born in the heavens; great wealth shall never cease,
and one shall constantly experience bliss until the very end of saṃsāra.
And thus realize the dharma of quiescent extinction.
The Buddha spoke this Gāthā Sūtra, briefly clarifying the retribution of merit,
so that all may universally give rise to faith and acceptance.
Auspiciousness illuminates the great earth; The full moon shines through the night, able to open the blue lotus flowers;
Śakra, Nārāyaṇa, and the foremost of all the devas—
Both are obtained through the practice of giving;
it illuminates universally from above to below, sustaining the lives of all beings,
yet even when the time arrives, it is impermanent.
And even for the hosts of devas, when their merit and lifespan are exhausted,
they enter the mouth of the enemy of death; consumed by the fires of grief, sorrow, and affliction,
they find no rest as they are burned.
Contemplate this impermanent body; Distance yourself from the thirst of desire.
Do not indulge in the pleasures of humans or devas, For they are but momentary and do not last long;
All things ultimately return to dissolution and decay.
Abandoning illusory pleasures, always go before the Buddha;
with palms joined, draw near to him, and through your own great enlightenment,
become a lord of liberation.
One Hundred Verses on the Collection of the Noble Ones (Āryasatya-gāthā-śataka)
